extraction.name: Visual Genome
extraction.description: A dataset of images densely annotated with numerous region descriptions, objects, attributes, and relationships to enable the modeling of interactions and relationships between objects in an image.
extraction.creator: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bemstein, Li Fei-Fei
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected and verified entirely by crowd workers from Amazon Mechanical Turk through a pipeline involving multiple task stages for creating descriptions, questions and answers, or region graphs.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 108,249 images from the intersection of the YFCC100M and MS-COCO datasets.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Collected over the course of 6 months after 15 months of experimentation.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases were canonicalized to WordNet synsets to reduce ambiguity.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text preprocessing included lowercasing, lemmatizing, stripping excess whitespace, and removing non-alphanumeric characters.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Workers were asked to draw bounding boxes and write descriptions for regions, extract objects, add attributes, and connect pairs of objects with relationships. They also wrote question-answer pairs.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Annotations were verified using majority voting (requiring 2 out of 3 workers to agree) and rapid judgments to eliminate incorrect, vague, or subjective labels.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: An average of 42 region descriptions, 21 objects, 18 attributes, 18 pairwise relationships, and 17 question-answer pairs per image.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 33,000 unique workers. 93.02% from the United States. Majority aged 25-34. 54.15% male and 45.85% female.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes demographic information collected from the crowd workers, specifically age, gender, and geographic location. Additionally, the image annotations contain human attributes such as gender (e.g., man, woman, male, girl) and age-related terms (e.g., young, teenager).
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset has a bias towards images of people and certain sports like skiing and surfboarding.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Mappings to WordNet synsets are not perfect and contain ambiguity. The dataset also lacks global scene descriptions compared to MS-COCO.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and benchmarking computer vision models for comprehensive scene understanding, cognitive tasks, image search, question answering, and robotic interactions.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: Visual Genome was collected and veried entirely by crowd workers from Amazon Mechanical Turk. In this section, we outline the pipeline employed in creating all the components of the dataset. Each component... involved multiple task stages.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: Visual Genome was collected and veried entirely by crowd workers from Amazon Mechanical Turk.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: The rst release of the Visual Genome dataset uses 108 ;249 images from the intersection of the YFCC100M (Thomee et al., 2016) and MS-COCO (Lin et al., 2014).

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: The dataset was collected over the course of 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: We canonicalize the objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases in region descriptions and questions answer pairs to WordNet synsets.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: First, we lowercase, lemmatize, and strip excess whitespace from all attributes... we remove all non-alphanumeric characters and lowercase and strip excess whitespace from them.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: When a new image is added to the crowdsourcing pipeline with no annotations, it is sent to a worker who is asked to draw three bounding boxes and write three descriptions for the region enclosed by each box... we present each worker with a region description along with its extracted objects and ask them to add attributes to objects or to connect pairs of objects with relationships

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: We used Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) as our primary source of annotations.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: All Visual Genome data go through a verication stage as soon as they are annotated... Verication is conducted using two separate strategies: majority voting (Snow et al., 2008) and rapid judgments... An annotation is added to our dataset if at least two (a majority) out of the three workers verify that it is factually correct.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: our dataset contains over 100K images where each image has an average of 21 objects, 18 attributes, and 18 pairwise relationships between objects... average a total of 42 region descriptions per image... average of 17 question-answer pairs

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: Overall, a total of over 33;000 unique workers contributed to the dataset... 93:02% of workers contributed from the United States... The majority of our workers were between the ages of 25 and 34 years old... near-balanced split of 54:15% male and 45 :85% female workers.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: we also use Stanford's dependency parser (Manning et al., 2014) to extract nouns automatically and send them to the workers as suggestions.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Our dataset is somewhat biased towards images of people, as Figure 13 shows... Certain sports (skiing ,surfboarding ) are overrepresented due to a bias towards these sports in our images.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: These mappings are not perfect and still contain some ambiguity... Out of all the descriptions gathered, only one or two of them tend to be global scene descriptions that are similar to MS-COCO

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: In this paper, we introduce the Visual Genome dataset with the aim of training and benchmarking the next generation of computer models for comprehensive scene understanding.
